transcript: 00:00 Marcus Li: Hey everybody, um thanks for joining. Welcome to the March all-hands. Quick reminder, we start on time, keep questions to the end, but feel free to drop in the chat. 00:22 Marcus Li: Okay Q1, short version — strong retention, two enterprise logos closed (healthcare and fintech), ARR growth roughly 18% quarter-over-quarter, more detail in the finance deck. 00:35 Hannah Greene: real quick on infra — we finished the kernel selection work for the Llama variants, there's still some perf delta on longer sequences but overall our throughput improved about 22% for typical chat workloads, uh this is with continuous batching tuned. 00:55 Priya Kapoor: yeah and to add, the KV cache optimizations reduced cold-start token cost; we're seeing fewer cache misses in prod, though a few edge cases with mixed model variants still cause regen. we'll follow up with a doc, link in #prod-updates. 01:20 Daniel Ortiz: product highlights for Q2 — top three bets: 1) rollout UI for canary/A-B, 2) cost-aware controls (batching/quant profiles surfaced to users), 3) private deployment experience polishing (VPC onboarding and HSM/KMS docs). we'll share the roadmap deck later today. 01:45 Audience (various): applause, yay 01:48 Samir Patel: on go-to-market — we landed a large healthcare customer after the security review; big shout to Lena and the solutions team for the SOC 2 evidence package, that made a difference. pipeline overall is healthy; we'll need 2 more reps for EMEA. 02:12 Lena Voss: security update, quick — SOC 2 readiness is on track, audit kickoff is scheduled for mid-April, we're still resolving a few minor findings around logging retention and SSO configs. KMS/HSM integrations doc is now v0.9, please send feedback. 02:35 Marcus Li: question from Slack — "Are customers shifting to Dedicated or Private?" 02:42 Samir Patel: short answer, mix; growth on Dedicated for customers wanting predictable throughput, Private for regulated workloads. trend-wise we're seeing hosted API still majority for dev/test. 03:02 Priya Kapoor: technical note — when customers switch to private or dedicated, we need to be clearer about the tradeoffs: latency vs cost, patching windows, and the ops model. there was a recent post-mortem where a private deploy had misconfigured KV cache and resulted in an hour-long degradation, we fixed it but it's a reminder to improve onboarding checklists. 03:36 Marcus Li: thanks Priya. quick applause for the infra team on the perf gains. 03:42 Audience (many): clapping 03:50 Daniel Ortiz: product question — how about function/tool calling and structure output for our customers? are we prioritizing that? 03:58 Priya Kapoor: yes, function calling improvements are prioritized — we'll add structured output validation in the canary flows so customers can opt in to stronger schema enforcement without changing their prompt layer. 04:20 Hannah Greene: ops update — SRE team increased on-call cover, new incident RCA template going out next week. also a note: we're adjusting autoscaling thresholds for Dedicated to reduce cost spikes during burst load. 04:45 Marcus Li: finance quick look — burn rate is stable, runway extended thanks to last month's enterprise commits, we did bump investment in reliability and hiring. 05:03 Samir Patel: sales highlights — two enterprise wins (healthcare and fintech), renewals in flight with three big customers, we're optimistic for Q2 expansion motions. 05:20 Audience: yay 05:26 Avery Chen: people update — hiring slowed a bit in Feb but we're ramping again, hiring priorities: infra, SRE, account execs in EMEA. couple HR items: parental leave policy update rolled out yesterday, and an all-company volunteering day planned for May. 05:46 Marcus Li: D&I — we've set an internal target to increase underrepresented engineers in mid-level hires by 20% this year; People will support with sourcing partnerships. 06:05 Marcus Li: quick product demo snippet — Daniel? 06:12 Daniel Ortiz: sure, very quick — demoed the canary rollout UI (slides), it's a small flow to pick two models, set traffic split, and configure automatic fallback to cheaper variant on error. note: this ties into routing policies. demo link in the notes. 06:40 Audience: good stuff 06:45 Priya Kapoor: a note on compatibility — fallback isn't universal because of kv cache layout differences across quantized variants; when fallback occurs you may see short regenerations. we plan to publish a compatibility matrix. 07:05 Marcus Li: ok moving to incidents — short post-mortem on the March 12th latency spike. Hannah? 07:12 Hannah Greene: summary — root cause was a kernel scheduling bug combined with a misapplied batch size change during a deploy; impact was increased p95 latency for about 40 minutes, we had increased server-side throttling which caused client retries, full RCA in #postmortems. remediation: revert change, backport kernel fix, and we added a pre-deploy perf smoke test to catch this. 07:46 Audience: mmhmm 07:50 Lena Voss: security follow-up — we improved audit logging and retention, partnered with Legal to update data retention policy; will share the redlined policy with Sales for customer questions. 08:10 Marcus Li: customer stories — Ethan, quick win? 08:16 Ethan Park: yes, healthcare customer reduced inference cost by about 30% by switching batching and applying quantization profile recommendations from Redwood Optimize; they were especially happy about the per-route cost breakdown in Console. 08:37 Audience: nice 08:40 Samir Patel: action item — Sales to package a bench-and-run offer for new pilots; we'll put a template in the playbook. 08:55 Marcus Li: org notes — leadership changes: Leah from Solutions becomes head of Enterprise Success next month, congrats. 09:05 Audience: clapping 09:10 Q&A: employee question about international regions — we plan more cloud regions in APAC by Q3, still sorting provider choices. 09:35 Employee (anon): question on compensation bands — People will hold an AMA next week. 09:50 Avery Chen: reminder: nominate people for awards, form in #people, due April 5th. 10:05 Marcus Li: final — recap of next steps and thanks. we blocked office hours for product/eng tomorrow for anyone with follow-ups. 10:22 Meeting ends. 10:25 Auto-generated notes: slides linked in #all-hands, roadmap deck and perf notes to be posted by EOD.
